Quantity, Date/Time, String equivalence, != (Not Equals), !~ (Not Equivalent). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release v2.0.0 §6.1.2 Equivalent, Quantity Equivalence: multi-item collections compare order-independently and each item must be equivalent; Quantity dimensions may match with different units.
issues.evidence: Fresh probe .temp/qa/fp13_skeptic_probe.py: component.value ~ referenceRange.high over Observation Quantity paths. Expected true because [1 cm, 2 cm] is equivalent order-independently to [0.02 m, 10 mm]. Native/C++ returned fhirpath_bool=false and [false]; forced Python fallback returned true.
issues.root_cause: Native multi-item equivalence used Quantity semantics only for literal FPValue::Quantity items. Resource-backed Quantity JSON values fell through to generic JSON equivalence; the first attempted conversion also lost JSON numeric source precision, causing incorrect equivalence tolerance and wrong item matching.
issues.resolution: Preserved JSON Quantity value source text in fpValueAsQuantity() and routed native multi-item equivalence through Quantity conversion/tolerance before generic JSON equivalence.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release v2.0.0 §6.1.2 Decimal Equivalence and §5.7.8 round(): Decimal equivalence rounds to the precision of the least precise operand; FHIRPath rounding says 0.5 or higher rounds up.
issues.evidence: Fresh probe .temp/qa/fp13_skeptic_probe.py: 1.25 ~ 1.2. Expected false because 1.25 rounded to one decimal place is 1.3, not 1.2. Native/C++ returned false; forced Python fallback returned true, indicating banker-rounding via Decimal.quantize default context.
issues.root_cause: Python fallback Decimal equivalence used Decimal.quantize() without specifying rounding mode and used Python round() for integer precision, so tie cases followed half-even instead of FHIRPath half-up rounding semantics.
issues.resolution: Changed Decimal equivalence rounding to use Decimal(str(value)).quantize(..., rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP) for both zero and non-zero precision.
